ticket.title: the unified workspace index and the root store index are the same sqlite file, so each command truncates the other view
ticket.description: Found 2026-11-10 while chasing why the benchwork panel showed 7 InProgress tickets.  THE SYMPTOM THAT NOTICED IT. The unified index held 7 InProgress rows; after a failed reap it held 169 rows instead of 365 - every member ticket gone from the panel. Nothing was lost on disk, but the view collapsed to one store.  THE CAUSE. StorypoleWorkspaceStore::open uses the ROOT STORE sqlite path for the unified index (workspace/store.rs, `open_and_sync_index(&rs.sqlite_path(), ...)`), while StorypoleStore::open rebuilds that same file from the root store ledger alone. So one file backs two different scopes and the last command to run decides which view it holds:  `storypole list` (root store)        -> 169 rows, harness tickets only  `storypole ledger-reconcile` (workspace) -> 365 rows, every store  Neither is wrong on its own; the file is the thing that cannot hold both. A panel reads whatever the previous command left, so it can show a partial board or a full one depending on unrelated activity, and a crash in the middle of a workspace sync leaves the partial view in place - which is exactly what was observed.  SUGGESTED SHAPE. Give the unified index its own file (e.g. `.gaugeblock/storypole/workspace.sqlite`) so a store-scoped command cannot truncate a suite view, or make the two scopes share one builder that always unions every store. Until then: run a workspace-scoped command (ledger-reconcile) after per-store work, and do not read the row count as evidence about the suite without knowing which command wrote it.
